```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# reserves blank work space (no ruled lines) for equation manipulation /
# show-your-work; pair with fig.height set to however much room is needed
blank_space <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
}
```

```{r key-helpers, include=FALSE}
ans_col <- rgb(200, 0, 130, maxColorValue = 255)
# redraws blank_table() so cells flagged TRUE in `ans` use the answer color
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, bold_rows = integer(0), ans = NULL) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      is_ans <- !is.null(ans) && isTRUE(ans[[i]][[j]])
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val, cex = cex,
                                    font = if (i %in% bold_rows) 2 else 1,
                                    col = if (is_ans) ans_col else "black")
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}
```

\ans{\textbf{Answer key.} Answers are in magenta.}


**NRES 746 -- Week 2, Lecture 1: R Syntax and Function Adjustments**

&nbsp;


&nbsp;

**Instructions:** Work alone on Parts 1-2 (about 10-12 minutes total).
Then get together with your neighbor(s) to compare answers.

## Part 1: Find the bug

Each snippet below has one bug. None of them are typos in the strict
sense -- the R is syntactically valid enough to run (or at least to try
to run). Circle the bug and write your fix directly on the snippet.

**1a.**

```

ricker <- function(a, b, x) {
  a * x * exp(-b * x)
}

# Evaluate the curve at x = 10, using a = 2, b = 0.5
ricker(10, 2, 0.5)

```

\ans{Arguments are in the wrong order: use \texttt{ricker(a = 2, b = 0.5, x = 10)} (or \texttt{ricker(2, 0.5, 10)}).}

**1b.**

```

a <- 2; b <- 0.3
curve(a * x * e^(-b * x), from = 0, to = 15)

```

\ans{R has no constant \texttt{e}; use \texttt{exp(-b * x)}.}

**1c.** 

```
ricker <- function(x, a, b = 0.2) a * x * exp(-b * x)
avals <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5)
peak_vals <- sapply(avals, ricker(), x = 5)

```

\ans{Pass the function itself, not a call to it: \texttt{sapply(avals, ricker, x = 5)}.}

## Part 2: Write it yourself

The base function $y = \sin(x)$ has period $2\pi$, ranges from $-1$ to
$1$, and increases fastest right where it crosses its midline ($y=0$)
heading upward -- at $x=0$ (and every $2\pi$ after that).

**2a.** Write the equation $y(t)$ (`t` = day of year, 1-365), built
from $\sin$, whose output:

- repeats with a period of exactly 1 year (365 days)
- ranges from 0 to 10
- increases fastest at $t = 91$ (April 1)

$y(t) =$ \ans{$5 + 5\sin\left(\frac{2\pi (t - 91)}{365}\right)$}



**2b.** Now translate your equation into an R function
`seasonal <- function(t) { ... }`.

\ansbegin

```
seasonal <- function(t) {
  5 + 5 * sin(2 * pi * (t - 91) / 365)
}
```

\ansend

**2c.** Name a real natural phenomenon this function could plausibly
approximate, and justify your choice in a sentence or two.

\ans{E.g., seasonal air or water temperature in the Northern Hemisphere: it warms fastest in spring, peaks near July 1 ($t \approx 182$), and is lowest near January 1. (Day length, or plant productivity, also works.)}
